checks.evidence: INL news release, 2026-10-06: DOE's Idaho Operations Office approved MARVEL's final documented safety analysis, authorizing a dry criticality configuration at near-zero power. The primary coolant system arrived at INL's Transient Reactor Test Facility in mid-September, and criticality 'is anticipated to occur in December' (2026). Older INL material from March 2026 and December 2025 coverage gave a 2027 dry-criticality target, so the release is the latest dated statement found.

sources.label: Idaho National Laboratory: MARVEL reactor gets federal safety approval as its primary vessel arrives in Idaho (Oct. 6, 2026)
sources.quote: before it achieves criticality, which is anticipated to occur in December

checks.review: Overruled 2026-11-12 (main session): dry criticality at near-zero power (Dec 2026) and 'operational' for end-user experiments (late 2027) are different events, so the shipped date is not contradicted. The December 2026 dry-criticality date was added to the row's timeline by hand with the INL release as a second source.

applications.name: Steady Energy and Alva-yhtiöt, Jyväskylä district heating study
applications.power_class: 100 MW to 300 MW of heat (2 to 6 LDR-50 units at 50 MWt each)
applications.timeline: Letter of intent announced 2026-05-19; a year-long preliminary study, then possible technical and commercial pre-planning
applications.sponsor: Alva-yhtiöt, the water and energy group of the City of Jyväskylä
applications.what_it_says: Steady Energy and Alva-yhtiöt signed a letter of intent to study whether an underground LDR-50 plant can supply the city's district heat. The companies said the city could be supplied with two to six units producing 100 MW to 300 MW of heat, and Alva said it is not yet making an investment decision. The study covers regulation, residents' views, sites, land use, technology and costs; no price and no current heat source are published.
applications.microreactor_read: Not a 1-20 MW buyer: one LDR-50 is 50 MWt and the study covers two to six of them. It is a district-heat reference point, and the open items are the year-long study and the investment decision.

sources.label: POWER Magazine: More Nuclear-Powered District Heating Planned in Finland (May 21, 2026)
sources.quote: it could supply Jyväskylä with between two and six LDR-50 reactors

items.headline: Canada seeks industry input on lunar microreactor technologies
items.what_happened: The Canadian Space Agency issued a request for information on lunar microreactor technologies, using a planning envelope of 20 kWe to 80 kWe of continuous net output and at least 10 years of life. It lists 16 areas of interest, from fuel and heat transport to launch integration, and says Canada is not assuming one domestic firm would deliver a full system.
items.why_it_matters: This is lunar power, not a terrestrial 1-20 MW buyer. It names no reactor type, no vendor and no buyer, so it signals interest in Canadian supply chains rather than demand.
items.binding_note: A request for information, not a contract. The release names no award and no selected technology.

sources.label: ANS Nuclear Newswire: Canada assesses its space reactor capabilities (Nov. 9, 2026)
sources.quote: lunar reactor capable of producing 20 kWe
